cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Retroactive Permission
cards.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like your agreement to dinner for six. We can serve it as a buffet; seated service needs more than two chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, people can stand with the soup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with bowls and nowhere to put them. I've invited them for seven, so I'll change the soup to something they can eat with one hand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. The invitations are settled; the menu is correctable. Can I have your yes while there is still time to cook?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 compares buffet and seated service, A3 corrects standing soup and A5 treats menu as the remaining adjustable detail to seek late consent.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 soup proposal causes A3 food correction; B4 already-invited question causes A5 admission, but seven can be read as count rather than time beside six.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a plausible but awkward serving plan and B4 asks about consent timing.

heightening.evidence: A5 asks for a genuine yes after completed invitations and before cooking, preserving retrospective approval.

specificity.evidence: A1 six guests and A3 for seven risks a needless headcount ambiguity.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 should name oclock so no reader must infer which of the two numbers is time.

coach2.missing: Seven should explicitly be a time, not an inferred headcount change.
coach2.firstDefect: A3 seven without oclock beside A1 six.
